summary: Describes a method of distributing a Multicast Address Resolution Server service within a logical IP subnet, using the Server Cache Synchronization Protocol to keep server databases in step. It is an experimental specification.

eli5.summary: If several helpers answer the same questions, they must share notes so they give the same answers. This says how helpers on an ATM network do that.

questions: how does scsp synchronize mars servers
how does distributed mars keep servers in sync
what is scsp and how does it work with mars
how do mars servers detect failure
subtitle: Keeping multiple multicast address servers in sync across an ATM subnet

tldr.problem: A single Multicast Address Resolution Server (MARS) for a logical IP subnet is a bottleneck and single point of failure. Multiple servers are needed, but they must stay synchronized to give consistent answers to all clients.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC specifies how to use the Server Cache Synchronization Protocol (SCSP) to replicate MARS databases across multiple servers in the same subnet. Clients register with any server in the group, and registration information is automatically shared to all other servers.
tldr.outcome: Distributed MARS allows fault tolerance and load distribution in ATM multicast networks. The solution depends on SCSP, which itself was specialized for MARS at the same time this RFC was written.

today: RFC 2443 is an Experimental protocol specification. ATM networks and the multicast services they required have largely faded from production use, making this protocol historically significant but not deployed in modern networks.

sections.title: The Distributed MARS Model
sections.content:
MARS (Multicast Address Resolution Server) manages layer 3 multicast services over ATM networks. A MARS server distributes layer 3 group membership information to clients in a logical IP subnet (LIS). Three types of entities participate: the MARS Server itself, which manages the group database; MARS Clients, which register with a single MARS and ask for group information; and MCS Clients (Multicast Servers), which register and offer to forward multicast traffic for specific groups.

When a single MARS server controls an entire LIS, it becomes a bottleneck and single point of failure. The RFC proposes allowing multiple MARS Servers in the same LIS, with SCSP (Server Cache Synchronization Protocol) keeping their databases in sync. Clients still register with only one MARS, but that MARS knows about all other servers and shares registration information across the group.
sections.eli5: A MARS server is like a phone directory for multicast groups on an ATM network. Instead of having one directory, you can have several, and they all share the same information so every answer is correct.

sections.title: Server Groups and Synchronization
sections.content:
All MARS Servers in a LIS form a Server Group (SG), identified by a Server Group ID (SGID). Each server sends SCSP protocol packets with a Protocol ID set to 0x0003 to mark them as MARS-specific. When a MARS Client or MCS Client registers with one server, that server sends a synchronization message to its peers in the SG. The peer servers update their own databases to reflect the new registration.

The RFC assumes each MARS Server in an SG is pre-configured with a unique range of Cluster Member IDs (CMIs) to assign to clients. The LIS boundary defines the SCSP server group boundary: all servers in the same LIS share one group. When a client detects MARS Server failure, it moves to the next MARS Server in a configured backup list and re-registers, including all its previous group memberships.
sections.eli5: Each helper (MARS Server) keeps a list of numbers it can give out to clients. When a client signs up with one helper, that helper tells all the other helpers so they know about it too.

sections.title: Cache Synchronization Records
sections.content:
SCSP exchanges information through Cache Synchronization Address (CSA) Records, each with a Protocol-Specific Part tailored to MARS. The CSA record carries hardware type (set to ATM Forum address family 15), protocol type (e.g., IPv4 is 0x0800), SNAP extension, version, and state. State values indicate the type of update: MARS Server Redirect Entry (heartbeat), MCS Serve/Register, MARS Client Join/Register, MARS Client Leave/Deregister, or MCS Unserve/Deregister.

Each record includes the source protocol address, source ATM address and subaddress, and for group operations, minimum and maximum multicast group addresses. The Cluster Member ID uniquely identifies the endpoint within the LIS. When servers receive these records, they update their caches to match, ensuring all servers have identical views of client registrations and group memberships.
sections.eli5: When one helper learns about a client, the helper sends a note to all other helpers saying "here's a client I just heard from, with these details." The note has special fields for ATM addresses and group numbers.

sections.title: Server Heartbeats and Failure Detection
sections.content:
Each MARS Server periodically sends a MARS Server Redirect Entry (a heartbeat message) to other servers in the SG, at least every 2 minutes (recommended every 1 minute). These messages tell peer servers that the sender is alive and provide the sender's ATM address. If a server fails to receive two consecutive heartbeats from a peer within the expected interval, it assumes that peer has crashed and flushes all client and group information learned from that failed server.

When a client unexpectedly disconnects from a server's CCVC (Cluster Control VC) or SCVC (Server Control VC), the server sends a proxy deregister message to all peers. This ensures that if a client crashes without notifying its MARS Server, all other servers learn of the disconnection. The surviving servers then clean up any cached information about that client.
sections.eli5: Helpers regularly say "I'm still here" to each other. If a helper stops saying that, the others know it crashed and forget about the clients it was serving. If a client suddenly disappears, a helper tells the others so they forget about it too.
